items.resolution: The paragraph limits the contribution to a typed, queryable evidence schema and the measured routing case. It does not claim judge calibration or Engine scheduling authority, and preserves thin telemetry for simple deployments.

The text states that the ideal centralized Bayes comparator observes the same exogenous signals and records the bounded-loss, ancillary-randomization conditional-independence and common-evidence assumptions. It excludes a claim that a fixed-budget single Agent can simulate any real DAG while preserving legitimate information, tool and authority splits.

The paragraph limits the no-escape result to the stated finite or local continuous kernel-threshold class, distinguishes theorem existence from magnitude, and presents exact, symbolic and hybrid approaches plus consolidation and verification as paid alternatives rather than universal cures.

Passed after correction: exact-v1 Sections 3.2 through 3.4 contain the GPU-CPU sparse-attention design, layer-ahead pre-computation and asynchronous KV recall, while Section 4.3 carries the performance evaluation. The Daily, queue and Books boundary now preserve the GPU as final state authority, bind benefits to host and interconnect conditions, and retain ordinary GPU attention as fallback.

Passed after correction: exact-v1 Section IV defines FSE-DP and Micro-Slice Flow, Section V defines the scheduling algorithm and scheduler hardware, and Section VI-C carries the end-to-end ablation evidence. The Daily, queue and Books text keep the router authoritative, treat the trajectory predictor as prefetch order only, bind claims to the chiplet and low-batch setting, and retain resident expert parallelism as fallback.

The chapter describes continuous synthetic KV as a learned state approximation, separates the training objective from serving-time ownership, and preserves query-distribution drift, validation and fallback as explicit costs rather than presenting compression as exact reuse.

The writeback assigns worker trajectory state to the scheduler and placement controller, keeps the evidence tied to the evaluated cluster and trace assumptions, and preserves simpler static placement when churn and prediction value are low.

The text treats the switch-centric controller as a bounded topology and collective-scheduling alternative, records the FPGA, simulator and eight-GPU evidence context, and does not generalize the measured result into a universal replacement for host- or GPU-controlled execution.
